plan.english: The great hero harnessed the swift horses, and they went to the dragon's field. Then the dragon saw the hero and was afraid. Then the hero hurled his spear at the dragon, and the dragon died. So the hero won imperishable fame.

Two brothers harnessed the swift horses. The first drove the chariot, the other hurled his spear. The earth trembled under the wheels. An enemy stood before them and said, "Where are you going, brothers?" The first answered, "We are seeking fame." Then the other killed the enemy.

The king gave the hero a gift. The hero said, "King, I will bring you the head of the wolf." Then he went out into the night. The wolf heard the hero and ran against him. But the hero seized the wolf and split its head. He carried the head to the king. The king said, "Your name is famous."

The warriors came to the settlement at night. One man broke the door and the other threw fire into the home. The fire burned, and they cried out. The king stood in the door and said, "I am not afraid of fire, and I will not flee from men." Then the king killed the first of the warriors, and the others fled.

Dawn became bright, and the wheel of the sun rose over the earth. The hero rose, yoked the horses to the yoke, and said, "Swift horses, carry me to the battle!" The horses heard the hero's word and ran forward. The wheels rolled, and the earth trembled.

A man stole the king's cattle in the night. The shepherd cried out and told the hero. The hero said, "Where are the cattle? I will find them." He yoked his horses and followed his path. At dawn he saw the man and the cattle. He hurled his spear, and the man died. Then the hero led the cattle to the king's home.

The wounded hero lay on the earth. His brother came and sat beside him. The hero said, "Brother, I shall die, but my fame will live. Take my spear, brother, and do not cry out." Then the hero died, and his name became famous.

title: The hero calls on the gods

plan.english: The hero stood on the field and called out to the gods. "Father Sky, hear me! Give me good fame and swift horses. Perkʷunos, you who hurled the spear at the serpent, be friendly to me." Then the gods heard the hero's word, and he went forth and was not afraid. He won great fame.

A wild horse stood in the hero's field. No one had yoked it. The hero came, looked at the horse, and said, "I shall yoke you. You will carry me, and I will give you water." The horse stood up and the hero harnessed it. Then they went forth, and the horse's name became famous.

The shepherd was guarding the sheep in the field. Wolves came out of the night. The shepherd was afraid and called to the hero: "Hero, come! The wolves are eating my sheep." The hero, grasping a spear, ran to the field and killed the wolves. Then the shepherd said, "You are a good man, and your name is famous."

Three heroes came to the sea. The sea was broad, and it was getting dark. Then the first said, "Brothers, do not tremble. We shall go over the sea and seek fame." They went into the night. The sea swallowed them, but their fame is imperishable.

The hero came home at dawn. His wife saw him at the door and cried out, "Husband, you have come! Our son has grown. Where were you?" The hero answered, "I bring you gifts and fame. Sit down, wife, and eat." Then she became glad, and they were sitting by the fire.

title: The king who broke his oath

plan.english: Two kings made an oath by the sky. The first kept the oath, but the other lied and took his cattle. Then the first said to him, "You who broke the oath, you shall not live. My spear will find you." He hurled the spear, and that king died.

title: The naming of the king's son

plan.english: A son was born to the king. The king took him in his arms and said, "I shall give you a name." "May your name be great, and may your fame be imperishable. Father Sky, protect him." Then the gods heard the king's word.

"Who are you, and where are you going?" the hero said to the stranger. The stranger answered, "I am the son of a king, and my name is famous. Go away from my path, hero!" The hero said, "I shall not go away. The path is broad. If you seek my death, stand up and take your spear." They hurled their spears, and the stranger sank down and died.

The first hero said to the other, "Hear me! My horses are swift, and my wheels are strong. Let us drive to the sea. Whoever arrives at the sea will take the prize." The other answered, "You speak many words, but I do not speak, I drive. Yoke your horses!" They yoked the horses, and the earth trembled under the wheels. The other reached the sea and took the prize. He said, "Good fame is my prize."

Many warriors stood on the field. A hero stepped out in front and cried, "Who will come against me? My spear has killed many men. I fear no one." Then another hero answered from the crowd, "Your words are many, hero, but my spear will speak." He came against him, and the first hero fell. The warriors cried out.

The hero stood and cried out to the dragon, "Serpent, hear my words! I am a hero, and my spear is swift. You devour cattle and sheep, and you are the enemy of men. Come forth, or I shall come to you!" The dragon came out and said, "Many heroes died by my fang. You will die." The hero hurled his spear, and the dragon's head was split. So the hero won good fame.

The king said to the hero, "Give me your horses and cattle, or I shall take them and burn your home." The hero heard the king's word and answered, "I will not give you my horses, and my cattle will not go to your field. If you come against me, you will see my spear." The king came with his warriors, but he saw the hero's spear and fled.

Two brothers were sitting by the fire and drinking. The first said, "I am the first and I am strong. I shall take our father's spear." The other answered, "You are the first, but I killed the wolf, and my name is famous. Stand up, brother, and take your spear." The mother came to the door and cried out, "Son, do not strike your brother! Is the field not broad?" The brothers heard her and put down the spears.

The enemy fled from the field, and the hero cried after him, "Where are you going, you who spoke many words yesterday? Now your heart trembles. Stand up and take your spear!" The enemy answered, "I shall not stand, for I shall live." The hero said, "Go, then. Whoever flees, his name is not famous."

Two men stood in the field. The first said to the other, "You stole my cattle." The other said, "I did not steal." The first said, "Then swear the oath by Father Sky." The other swore the oath and said, "If I lie, may Father Sky kill me." But he was lying. Father Sky heard, and in the night the man died.

A wolf came to the sheep in the night. The dog heard him, stood up, and said, "Wolf, I guard the shepherd's sheep. Go away, or you will see my fangs." The wolf answered, "You are the shepherd's dog, but I am free. You work for a man, and I work for no one." The dog said, "The shepherd feeds me, but you tremble in the night." The wolf went away into the night.

Two heroes sat by the fire before the king. The first said, "I killed seven wolves in the night." The other said, "I killed a serpent. It devoured cattle and men." The king heard them and said, "You are both heroes. To the first I give a spear, to the other I give a horse. Both of you have won fame."

The hero said to his enemy, "At dawn I shall stand on the field. Come with your spear." The enemy answered, "I shall come. May the sun see us." Dawn became bright, and the two stood on the field. They hurled their spears, and the enemy sank down and died.

Two heroes came to the field. The first cried out, "Who are you? I do not know you." The other answered, "I am the son of the man who was a guest in your father's home." The first said, "Then you are my guest, and I will not kill you. Put down your spear, and let us give gifts. Take my horses, and I shall take your spear." So they gave gifts, and their names became famous.

A strong man stood at the door of the settlement. He cried out, "Whoever comes to this door will see my spear." Then the hero of good fame came to the door. He said, "Stand aside from the door, or I shall break it." The strong man did not stand aside. The hero hurled his spear, and the strong man fell. Then the hero broke the door and went into the settlement.

title: The hero takes leave of his wife

plan.english: The hero stood at the door and said to his wife, "Wife, I am going out from our home, and I shall seek fame. Stay in the home, and guard our son. Do not cry for me. The sun comes back each day, and I shall come back. May Mother Earth guard you." Then he went out into the dawn, and his wife stood in the door.

title: A father's words to his son

plan.english: The father said to his son, "Hear my words, son. Do not lie to your guest, and do not flee from the spear. If you do this, your fame will be great. Now go, and may the gods protect you." The son heard his father's word and went away.

The mother said to her son, "Son, you are going to the spears, and my heart trembles. Wear this clothing. Remember your mother's words." The son answered, "Mother, do not cry. I shall come back with fame, and you will hear my name." Then the son went out, and the mother stood at the door.

The sister came to the door and cried out, "Brother, where are you going?" The brother answered, "Sister, I am going over the sea." She said, "Drink the water, brother, and take this gift. Remember your sister. May Father Sky guard your path, and come back with good fame." He drank the water, took the gift, and went.

title: The dying king and his sons

plan.english: The king lay down, and his sons came to him. He said, "Sons, I leave you my spears and my horses. Be brothers, and do not break the oath. When a son is born to you, set my name on him. Sleep is coming to me." Then the king died, and his sons cried out.

title: The hero takes leave of his horses

plan.english: The hero led his horses to the field and spoke to them, "Swift horses, you who carried me for many nights, now lie down in the field. Eat the grain, and drink the water. No one shall yoke you." The horses looked at him, and the hero went away.

title: The hero leaves his son to the gods

plan.english: In the night the hero went out and cried to Father Sky and Mother Earth, "Hear me, you gods! I give you my son. Guard him in the field and in the home. If I die, let him hear my name, and let him say, 'The fame of my father is good.'"

title: The exile leaves his father's house

plan.english: The man left his home in the night. He stood at the door and cried out, "My father's door! My father's fire! My father's field! I go away, and I shall not come back. May the gods guard you, and may no one burn you."

The hero's wife answered him at the door, "Go, husband. I shall guard the fire, and our son will grow. Remember your home. May your spear be swift, and may your horses be swift. Come back to me with good fame."

title: The last night before the spears

plan.english: Two warriors were sitting by the fire in the night. The first said to the other, "At dawn the spears will speak. If I die, tell my mother, 'He did not flee.' The other answered, "I shall tell her. Your name is famous." They drank, and they lay down by the fire.

The hero stood at the door and spoke to the dog, "Dog, you who guarded my door in the night, sit down at the door. Guard my wife and my son. May the wolf not come to the door. I go to seek fame, and I shall come back." The dog heard him and lay down at the door.

Dawn became bright, and the hero, grasping his spear, yoked the horses. His brothers stood around him and said, "May the wheel of the sun go before you. May you win great fame." The hero said, "Brothers, guard our father's home." Then the horses ran forward, and the brothers stood at the door.

The sons laid their father on the fire. The fire burned, and they spoke, "Go, father, by the path of the sun. May Mother Earth receive you. Your fame is imperishable. We shall set your name on our sons." Then they went home.
